Test data seeded by backend suite (TEST_ITER611) visible in queue.

minor.issue: staff_surnames_db picks 'Manager', 'Housekeeper', 'Receptionist', 'Admin', 'Tester' as surnames (from users named 'Test Manager' etc.). Any response containing the word 'manager' (e.g. 'our general manager') is blocked as 'staff_private' → false positive privacy violation. staff_surnames_db should filter role/title words (manager, housekeeper, receptionist, admin, staff, team, management, director) or require last_name to be an actual person's surname.

Endpoint saves response_quality/similarity/decision/ai_candidates but does NOT persist generated_text into review.response_text. This makes it hard to feed a generated draft into the approval queue via /submit-for-approval (which requires response_text). Workaround: PUT /reviews/{id}/respond (which sets response_text but flips status→responded) then /submit-for-approval. Consider optionally persisting best candidate as response_text with status='pending_approval' when publishing_mode is 'smart_auto' or 'manual'.

ui_bugs.issue: Spec requires data-testid 'review-agent-btn' opening a ReviewAgentPanel with pubmode-manual/smart_auto/full_auto radios and rule-* inputs (min_rating, max_spam_pct, max_risk, min_quality, max_similarity, block_refund) + full_auto authoriser input + ra-save-config button. None of these testids exist on the page in any state. Sidebar has 'ai-reply-robot-btn' but clicking it navigates to the AI Reply Robot bulk-draft page (which does not expose publishing_mode/auto_rules UI). ReviewAgentPanel appears not to be wired into the navigation.

action_items: Filter role/title words from staff_surnames_db output (or require a distinct 'last_name' field not derived from split) to avoid privacy false-positives on the word 'manager' etc.
Wire ReviewAgentPanel into PRO sidebar with data-testid 'review-agent-btn' and expose pubmode-*/rule-*/ra-save-config testids so the publishing_mode + auto_rules config is reachable from the UI.

Consider persisting the best generated candidate as response_text (with status pending_approval) on POST /reviews/generate-ai-response, so /submit-for-approval flows work without hitting PUT /respond first.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/guests/reviews.py is ~1930 lines — should be split (widget, approval, CRUD, sentiment/analytics, competitors, templates, seed) for maintainability.

generate-ai-response saves ai_candidates but not response_text; approval queue requires response_text — this asymmetry forces callers to detour via PUT /respond (which itself flips status to 'responded' and fires outbound sync). Recommend explicit status=pending_approval on save.

privacy_check staff surname source is naive: last_name = split(name)[-1]; role words become surnames when seed users are named 'Test Manager', 'Test Receptionist'. Add a role-word blocklist or use dedicated last_name/family_name fields.

approve-bulk: uses cfg.auto_rules.min_quality (default 80) but risk-level check requires strict 'low' — good conservative gate; but there is no upper cap on total items processed (to_list(200)). For very large queues consider chunking + audit trail.
log_review_event: uses two update_one calls (init + push); could be one $push with $slice on a $ifNull-guarded field.
review_sources.py: 'mode':'simulated' returned when key missing OR business_unit_id missing — good; consider surfacing the reason ('no_api_key' vs 'no_bu_id') for admins.
review_agent.py config validator drops unknown auto_rules keys but silently — consider returning warnings for dropped keys so callers know 'bogus' was ignored.

rca of the issue: Privacy false-positive: staff_surnames_db in reviews.py line ~209 derives surnames from last_name OR split(name)[-1] on users/staff, without filtering role/title tokens. Seed data has users like 'Test Manager', 'Test Receptionist' → 'Manager', 'Receptionist' end up in the surname list. privacy_check then flags any response containing those role words (word-boundary regex) as staff_private, blocking legitimate published responses. Fix: (a) maintain an explicit ROLE_WORDS = {'manager','housekeeper','receptionist','admin','staff','team','management','director','concierge','host','owner'} filter in staff_surnames_db, or (b) require an explicit last_name field on user docs, ignoring split() heuristic.
